source_text: Ecce ergo planum est nos Christi gratiam utilem parvulis non negare. Quid igitur controversiae remansit, propter quod nos Traducianus erroris insimulat, videlicet quia non annuimus Adae quidem bonam, sed omnium hominum malam factam esse naturam? Hoc sane non solum nos non annuere, verum etiam et summis viribus impugnare profiteor. Remotis igitur illis figmentorum tuorum distortis pueriliter retibus et vulgaribus maniis, quibus susurrabas nos Christi gratiam negare cunabulis, super hoc congrediamur, in quo est summa certaminis. Eo igitur ordine, quem promisi, quia iam nostra defendi, Manichaei, cui te adversari simulabas, et vestra sensa pensemus.
pass_a_gloss: Behold therefore it is plain that we do not deny the grace of Christ useful to little ones. What therefore of controversy has remained, on account of which the advocate of inherited sin accuses us of error, namely because we do not nod that the nature of Adam indeed was made good, but of all humans evil? This indeed I profess not only that we do not nod, but even that we impugn with highest forces. With those childishly distorted nets of your inventions therefore removed and the vulgar bogeys by which you were whispering that we deny the grace of Christ to cradles, let us contend over this, in which is the sum of the struggle. In that order therefore which I promised, because already ours have been defended, let us weigh the senses of the Manichaean, whom you were simulating to be adverse to, and yours.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis

pass_b_english: It is therefore clear that we do not deny the benefit of Christ’s grace to infants. What controversy remains, then, for which the advocate of inherited sin accuses us of error? That we do not agree that Adam’s nature was made good but everyone else’s evil? I freely acknowledge that we not only refuse to agree but attack this with all our strength. Put aside, then, those childishly twisted nets of your inventions and the popular bogeys through which you whispered that we deny Christ’s grace to the cradle. Let us contend over the central issue of the dispute. Following the order I promised, now that I have defended our views, let us weigh yours and those of Mani, whom you pretended to oppose.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
